examples.ko: 아버지가 눈짓하자 동생은 조용히 입을 닫았어요.
examples.en: When Dad signaled with his eyes, my sibling quietly stopped talking.
My friend signaled with his eyes for me to go out.
The teacher signaled with her eyes for us to sit.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 동료에게 눈짓해서 신호를 보냈어요.
examples.en: During the meeting I sent a signal to a coworker with my eyes.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 문 쪽을 보며 눈짓하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is gesturing with his eyes toward the door.
Even though I signaled with my eyes not to say it, it was no use.

explain: 말 대신 눈으로 신호를 보낼 때 써요. 보통 '~라고 눈짓하다'로 내용을 붙이고, 같은 뜻으로 '눈짓을 하다', '눈짓을 보내다'도 많이 써요. 서로 신호를 주고받을 때는 '눈짓을 주고받다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The teacher gave me a signal with their eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈짓하다'와 같은 뜻이고 명사 '눈짓'을 따로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 눈짓하다, with the noun 눈짓 used separately.

phrases.en: My friend sent me a look to say let's go out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 신호를 전한다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of sending a signal to someone.

phrases.en: The two people exchanged glances.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 눈으로 신호를 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two people signal each other with their eyes.

explain_en: It is used when you send a signal with your eyes instead of words. The content is usually added as '~라고 눈짓하다', and '눈짓을 하다' or '눈짓을 보내다' work too. For exchanging signals, say '눈짓을 주고받다'.

en: to step aside; to move aside

examples.en: A car is coming, so please step to the left.

examples.ko: 구급차 소리가 들리면 길 옆으로 비켜나야 해요.
examples.en: When you hear an ambulance, you have to move to the side of the road.

examples.ko: 공사 중이니까 잠깐 옆으로 비켜나 계세요.
examples.en: Construction is going on, so please stay off to the side for a moment.
He quietly slipped away from the crowd.

examples.ko: 그 문제에서 한 발 비켜나서 생각해 보면 어때요?
examples.en: Why don't you step back from that problem and think about it?
When the children moved aside, a big truck passed through.

explain: '비키다'와 비슷하지만, 길을 내주려고 몸을 옮길 때는 '좀 비켜 주세요'처럼 '비키다'가 더 자연스러워요. '비켜나다'는 중심이나 길에서 벗어나 떨어진다는 느낌이라 '논란에서 비켜나다'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The people stepped aside to one side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방향을 말하는 말과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with a word for direction.
phrases.en_equiv: to step aside to one side

phrases.en: He is staying out of that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에서 떨어져 있는 상태를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of being away from some matter.

phrases.en: That singer stayed out of this controversy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 되는 일에 얽히지 않고 벗어난다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for staying clear of a troublesome matter.

explain_en: It is close to '비키다', but when asking someone to make way, '좀 비켜 주세요' with '비키다' sounds more natural. '비켜나다' feels like moving away from the center or the path, so it is also used figuratively, as in '논란에서 비켜나다' (to stay out of a controversy).

examples.ko: 뭐가 그렇게 좋아서 혼자 실실 웃어요?
examples.en: What's so good that you're grinning to yourself?

examples.ko: 그는 혼나는 중에도 실실 웃어서 더 화나게 했어요.
examples.en: He kept snickering even while being scolded, which made them angrier.

examples.ko: 실실 웃으면서 거짓말하는 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to trust someone who lies while smirking.

examples.ko: 동생이 실실 웃으며 제 방으로 들어왔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling came into my room grinning slyly.

examples.ko: 친구가 소개팅 얘기만 나오면 실실 웃기 시작해요.
examples.en: My friend starts grinning whenever a blind date comes up.

examples.ko: 그렇게 실실 웃지 말고 진지하게 말해 봐요.
examples.en: Stop grinning like that and speak seriously.

explain: 주로 '웃다'와 같이 써서 소리 없이 가볍게 웃는 모습을 나타내요. 칭찬보다는 장난스럽거나 속이 보이는 웃음을 흉보거나 놀릴 때 더 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 문자만 보면 실실 웃어요.
phrases.en: That friend snickers every time he looks at his texts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실실'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사로, 속이 보이는 웃음에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with 실실, fitting a smile that gives away what someone is thinking.

phrases.en: Why have you been snickering to yourself since earlier?
phrases.nuance_ko: '실실' 뒤에 '-거리다'를 붙여 계속 웃는 모습을 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -거리다 turns it into one verb meaning to keep snickering.

phrases.en: My younger sibling looked at me with a silly grin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실실'과 비슷하지만 입을 헤벌리고 웃는 모습에 더 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 실실 but closer to a wide, goofy grin.

explain_en: It is mainly used with '웃다' to show a light, quiet smile. It suits teasing or mildly criticizing a playful or smug grin more than praising someone.

examples.ko: 회사에서 직원에게 돈을 주고 입막음을 했대요.
examples.en: I heard the company paid the employee to keep quiet.
There's a rumor that the money was hush money.

examples.ko: 그 일은 입막음 때문에 알려지지 않았어요.
examples.en: That matter didn't become known because of the silencing.
I gave my little sibling snacks to keep them quiet.
Despite his efforts to silence people, the rumor spread.
Keeping people quiet wasn't easy, so I finally gave up.

explain: 돈, 선물, 부탁, 위협으로 다른 사람이 말하지 못하게 하는 일이라 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서는 '입막음용 돈'처럼 자주 나오고, 가볍게 비밀을 부탁할 때는 '비밀로 해 줘요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The company tried to buy the employee's silence with money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사에 '하다'를 붙인 동사로, 말하지 못하게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb made with 하다, meaning to make someone unable to speak.

phrases.en: There are allegations that hush money was paid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 돈으로 입을 막았다는 이야기를 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when money was allegedly paid for silence.

phrases.en: Please keep this between us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 비밀을 부탁할 때는 입막음 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The light, everyday way to ask for secrecy instead of 입막음.

explain_en: It means getting someone not to talk through money, gifts, requests or threats, so it has a somewhat negative tone. In the news you often see it as '입막음용 돈' (hush money), while for a light request to keep a secret people say '비밀로 해 줘요'.

examples.en: When I asked, my friend shook his head.

examples.ko: 아이는 싫다고 고개를 가로젓고 울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The child shook his head saying no and started to cry.
She waved her hand from side to side and said it was fine.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 고개를 가로저으셔서 걱정이 됐어요.
examples.en: The doctor shook his head, so I got worried.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 머리만 가로젓고 있었어요.
examples.en: He was just shaking his head without saying anything.

examples.ko: 제안을 들은 부장님이 고개를 가로젓지 않아서 안심했어요.
examples.en: The manager did not shake his head at the proposal, so I felt relieved.

explain: '고개를 가로젓다'의 모양으로 가장 많이 쓰고, '아니다, 싫다, 안 된다'는 뜻을 몸으로 보여 줄 때 써요. 반대로 '네'라는 뜻은 '고개를 끄덕이다'라고 해요. 'ㅅ' 불규칙이라서 '가로저어요, 가로저었어요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: He refused, shaking his head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~(으)며'로 연결해서 동시에 하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '~(으)며' links an action done at the same time.

phrases.en: I waved my hand and said it was fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손을 좌우로 흔들며 거절하거나 사양할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It also describes waving a hand side to side to decline.

phrases.en: If you like it, nod your head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가로젓다'와 반대로 '네'라는 뜻을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the opposite of 가로젓다 and shows yes.

explain_en: It mostly appears as '고개를 가로젓다' and shows 'no', 'I don't want to' or 'that's not OK' with a body gesture. The opposite, meaning 'yes', is '고개를 끄덕이다'. It is a ㅅ-irregular verb, so it becomes '가로저어요' and '가로저었어요'.

examples.en: There is a checkpoint at the highway entrance.
The police stopped the car at the checkpoint.

examples.ko: 검문소를 지날 때 신분증을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I showed my ID when passing the checkpoint.
There are many checkpoints near the border.

examples.ko: 검문소 앞에서 차가 길게 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: Cars lined up long in front of the checkpoint.

examples.ko: 검문소의 군인이 가방을 열어 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The soldier at the checkpoint told me to open my bag.

explain: 공항 보안 검색대나 입국 심사와는 달라요. 검문소는 도로나 국경 근처에서 차를 세우고 사람을 확인하는 곳이에요. '검문을 받다', '검문에 걸리다'처럼 '검문'과 같이 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: Right after you pass the checkpoint, there's the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 검문소를 통과한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means passing through a checkpoint on the road.

phrases.en: We were stopped and checked near the border.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차나 사람이 확인을 당할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a car or person is stopped and checked.

phrases.example: 검문소 앞에서 차가 길게 줄을 섰어요.
phrases.en: Cars lined up in a long row in front of the checkpoint.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 말할 때 '앞'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 앞 to talk about the spot in front of it.

explain_en: It differs from an airport security line or immigration. A '검문소' stops vehicles and checks people on roads or near borders. Learn it with '검문', as in '검문을 받다' and '검문에 걸리다'.

examples.ko: 이 문제에 대해 선생님의 고견을 듣고 싶어요.
examples.en: I would like to hear your valued opinion on this issue, teacher.
Before deciding, I asked the team leader for his valued advice.

examples.ko: 교수님 고견 덕분에 논문 방향을 잡았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the professor's valuable advice, I found the direction for my paper.
We need your valued opinions on this matter.

examples.ko: 부모님의 고견도 들어 보고 정하려고 해요.
examples.en: I plan to hear my parents' wise opinion too before I decide.

examples.ko: 고견은 언제든지 환영하니까 편하게 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: Your valued opinions are welcome any time, so please feel free to share.

explain: 상대방의 의견을 높여서 부르는 말이라 내 의견에는 쓸 수 없어요. 내 의견은 '제 의견'이라고 해요. 보통 '고견을 듣다', '고견을 구하다', '고견을 부탁드리다'처럼 회의나 편지 같은 격식 있는 자리에서 써요.

phrases.example: 이 계획에 대해 선생님의 고견을 부탁드려요.
phrases.en: I'd like to ask for your valuable opinion on this plan, teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 의견을 정중하게 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely request someone's opinion.

phrases.en: The professor shared his valuable opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 의견을 말해 준 일을 높여서 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to respectfully say that someone shared their opinion.

phrases.en: Thank you for your valuable opinion.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귀한'을 붙여 상대의 의견에 감사할 때 인사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 귀한 makes it a polite phrase of thanks for someone's opinion.

explain_en: It honors the other person's opinion, so you can never use it for your own; say '제 의견' (my opinion) instead. It appears in set phrases like '고견을 듣다', '고견을 구하다' and '고견을 부탁드리다', mostly in meetings and letters.

en: to be enraged; to be infuriated

examples.en: My father flew into a rage when he saw my report card.
The boss blew up when he found out about the mistake.
It's nothing to get that furious about.
He shouted furiously because the promise was broken.
My mom goes ballistic if I tell a lie.
The customer raged, and the shop was in an uproar.

explain: '화내다'보다 훨씬 세게, 펄펄 뛰며 크게 화내는 모습이에요. 아버지나 사장님 같은 윗사람이 화낼 때 어울리고, 높일 때는 '노발대발하세요/하셨어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: My grandfather hit the roof when he heard the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 크게 화낼 때는 '-시-'를 넣어 높여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Insert -시- to show respect when an elder is furious.

phrases.en: The teacher came into the classroom in a rage.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)며'로 화난 모습과 다른 행동을 함께 이어요.
phrases.nuance_en: -(으)며 links the angry state with another action.

phrases.en: He got very angry when he found out about the lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노발대발하다'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 바꿔 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 노발대발하다.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '화내다' and describes someone leaping with rage. It fits when a father, a boss or another superior gets angry, and the honorific forms are '노발대발하세요' and '노발대발하셨어요'.

examples.en: He toyed with people through his lies.
Please don't toy with my feelings.

examples.ko: 상대 팀을 농락하는 화려한 드리블에 관중이 환호했어요.
examples.en: The crowd cheered at the flashy dribbling that made fools of the other team.
A rumor went around that the boss was playing games with his employees.

examples.ko: 그들은 법을 농락하며 세금을 내지 않았어요.
examples.en: They made a mockery of the law and didn't pay their taxes.

examples.ko: 사람을 농락해서 얻은 성공은 오래가지 않아요.
examples.en: Success gained by toying with people doesn't last.

explain: 상대를 자기 마음대로 가지고 놀며 속이거나 이용한다는 느낌이 강한 말이에요. 단순히 '속이다'보다 상대를 바보로 만드는 비난의 느낌이 있어서, 나쁜 일을 한 사람을 말할 때 많이 써요. 당하는 쪽에서는 '농락당하다'라고 말하고, 스포츠에서 압도적으로 이길 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: I was played with by that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당하는 쪽에서 말하는 표현이고, 속아서 이용당했다는 억울한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the victim's side, with a sense of having been deceived and used.

phrases.en: Don't play with people's feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 농락하다와 비슷하게 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday phrase with a similar meaning.

phrases.en: He tried to toy with people using his words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으려고 하다'를 붙여 나쁜 의도로 시도했다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -으려고 하다 it shows an attempt with bad intent.

explain_en: It strongly suggests playing with someone as you like, deceiving or using them. Rather than just '속이다' (to deceive), it carries a critical sense of making a fool of the other person, so it is used for people who did something wrong. The victim's side is expressed as '농락당하다', and it is also used figuratively when a team wins overwhelmingly in sports.

examples.en: The dishes clatter against each other when I wash up.

examples.ko: 서랍 안에서 동전이 달그락 소리를 내요.
examples.en: The coins rattle inside the drawer.

examples.ko: 밤에 부엌에서 달그락 소리가 들려서 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up because I heard a clattering sound in the kitchen at night.
The child dropped the spoon with a clatter.

examples.ko: 열쇠 꾸러미가 가방 안에서 달그락 흔들려요.
examples.en: The bunch of keys rattles around in the bag.
I heard a clatter and turned around, and it was the cat.

explain: 작고 단단한 물건끼리 가볍게 부딪히는 소리예요. 더 크고 무거운 느낌은 '덜그럭'으로 말해요. 보통 '달그락 소리'나 '달그락거리다/달그락대다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I heard a clattering sound in the kitchen at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 물건이 부딪히는 소리를 명사처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the sound of small things knocking together.

phrases.en: The spoon touches the bowl and clatters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 소리를 계속 낸다는 뜻의 동사 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to keep making that sound.

phrases.en: The coins make a clinking sound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 여러 번 이어질 때 두 번 겹쳐서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeated when the sound goes on several times.

explain_en: It is the sound of small hard objects knocking lightly together. For a bigger, heavier sound, people say '덜그럭'. It is often used as '달그락 소리' or in '달그락거리다/달그락대다'.

examples.ko: 하늘에 흰 구름이 두둥실 떠 있어요.
examples.en: White clouds are floating gently in the sky.
The balloon floated up into the sky.
The full moon rose softly above the mountain.
A boat drifts lightly on the water.
The kids chased the soap bubbles floating away.

examples.ko: 튜브를 타고 바다에 두둥실 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: I lay floating on the sea in a tube.

explain: 구름, 달, 풍선, 배처럼 가볍게 떠 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요. '둥둥'보다 부드럽고 편안한 느낌이라 '떠 있다', '떠오르다'와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The full moon rose gently into the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달이나 풍선이 부드럽게 올라오는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits the moon or a balloon rising softly.

phrases.example: 배가 호수 위에 두둥실 떠 있어요.
phrases.en: A boat is floating gently on the lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 떠서 머물러 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something floating lightly and staying there.

phrases.en: Clouds drift lazily along.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 이리저리 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes slow movement here and there.

explain_en: It describes things like clouds, the moon, balloons and boats floating lightly. It feels softer and more relaxed than '둥둥' and goes well with '떠 있다' and '떠오르다'.

examples.en: A cloud is floating in the sky.
The balloon floated away on the wind.
The moon rose softly over the mountain.

examples.ko: 물 위에 오리가 둥실 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A duck is floating on the water.
The boat sways gently on the river.
We floated and played in the sea on an inner tube.

explain: 가볍고 부드럽게 떠 있거나 떠오르는 모습이에요. '둥실둥실'이나 '두둥실'처럼 늘여서 쓰면 더 느긋하고 시적인 느낌이 나요.

phrases.example: 호수 위에 오리 인형이 둥실둥실 떠 있어요.
phrases.en: A toy duck is floating on the lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: '둥실'을 반복해서 계속 떠 있는 모습을 더 느긋하게 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Repeating 둥실 shows something floating on and on in a more relaxed way.

phrases.en: The full moon rose up softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '둥실'을 늘인 말로, 시나 노래처럼 더 시적이고 여유로운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stretched form of 둥실 with a more poetic, leisurely feel, like in poems and songs.

phrases.example: 아침 해가 바다 위로 둥실 떠올랐어요.
phrases.en: The morning sun rose lightly over the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가가 가볍게 위로 올라오는 모습을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for something rising lightly upward.

explain_en: It describes floating or rising lightly and softly. Stretched forms like '둥실둥실' or '두둥실' sound more relaxed and poetic.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁 뒷간은 마당 끝에 있었어요.
examples.en: The outhouse at my grandmother's house was at the end of the yard.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 밤에 뒷간 가는 게 무서웠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, going to the outhouse at night was scary.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기에는 뒷간 귀신이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Outhouse ghosts often appear in old tales.
The smell is quite strong in a country outhouse.
Grandfather said he was going to the outhouse and went out.
These days people say "restroom" instead of "outhouse."

explain: 집 밖에 따로 있던 옛날식 변소를 말해요. 지금은 '화장실'이라고 하고, 뒷간은 시골 이야기나 옛이야기, 속담에서 주로 만나요.

phrases.ko: 뒷간 갈 적 마음 다르고 올 적 마음 다르다
phrases.example: 뒷간 갈 적 마음 다르고 올 적 마음 다르다더니, 도와 달라던 사람이 인사도 없네요.
phrases.en: One's attitude changes once one's need has been met.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급할 때와 일이 끝난 뒤의 태도가 달라지는 사람을 꼬집는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb that points out people who act differently when they need help and after the need is gone.
phrases.en_equiv: change one's tune once one's needs are met

explain_en: It refers to the old-style toilet that stood separately outside the house. Today people say '화장실', and 뒷간 is mostly met in countryside stories, old tales and proverbs.
